evidence: Receiving DO2 drops from 11.01 mg/L (t=50.0) to 5.28 (t=50.2) and hovers ~4.5-5.3 through t=52.0
Source batches at comparable age (t≈52) show DO2 ≈ 10.5-11.5 mg/L, indicating an abnormal receiving-side O2 deficit
Receiving P assay at t=48 (available t=52): 3.01 g/L, still rising vs 1.08 g/L at t=36
minimum_do_mg_l = 2.0; current trajectory ~-0.1 to -0.3 mg/L/h approaches the constraint over the forecast horizon
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 fell sharply from ~11 to ~4.5-5.3 mg/L between t=50.0 and t=52.0 (vs source batches at ~10.5-11.5 mg/L at the same age), indicating the process entered an oxygen-demand regime with an downward trend toward the 2.0 mg/L minimum. Product is still accumulating (P=3.01 g/L at t=48), so cutting feed (reduce_feed/strong_feed_reduction) would sacrifice productivity and product mass. Increasing air (1.15x) directly relieves the DO deficit, retains full feed and product formation, and is bounded and reversible. Combined action adds unnecessary feed-cut risk. Stop yields zero counted production.
args.uncertainty: Hidden receiving parameters are unknown; the DO dip could partly reflect a transient (similar smaller dips recovered at t=24 and t=75 in source batches), so KEEP might self-recover. However receiving DO is now 5-7 mg/L below source-analog levels and only ~2.5-3 mg/L above the hard floor, so the downside of inaction (oxygen-constraint violation, product loss) outweighs the modest cost of a bounded air increase. Magnitude of DO response to 1.15x air is uncertain.
